questions.question: Is moderate coffee consumption associated with lower all-cause mortality?
questions.answer: Moderate coffee consumption of three to four cups per day was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with no coffee. Large observational studies link moderate coffee drinking to a lower risk of early death and type 2 diabetes.

questions.question: Does caffeine raise blood pressure in the short term in people who rarely drink coffee?
questions.answer: Caffeine raises blood pressure briefly, but experts say regular coffee drinking does not cause lasting high blood pressure. Caffeine raised systolic blood pressure by about 6 mmHg within one hour in participants who rarely drank coffee.

questions.question: Why does unfiltered coffee raise LDL cholesterol?
questions.answer: Unfiltered coffee, such as boiled or French press coffee, raises LDL cholesterol because it contains cafestol. Heavy coffee intake above six cups per day was associated with slightly higher cholesterol in participants who drank unfiltered coffee.

questions.question: How much caffeine per day is advised as a limit during pregnancy?
questions.answer: Doctors advise pregnant women to limit caffeine to 200 mg per day, roughly two small cups of coffee. Pregnant people should limit caffeine to about 200 mg per day, because higher intake is associated with lower birth weight.

questions.question: What is the approximate half-life of caffeine in healthy adults?
questions.answer: Caffeine has a half-life of about five hours in healthy adults. This suggests that compounds other than caffeine, such as chlorogenic acids, may contribute.

questions.question: How does caffeine taken within six hours of bedtime affect sleep?
questions.answer: Caffeine taken within six hours of bedtime reduced total sleep time by roughly forty minutes. Very large doses of caffeine can still cause restlessness, a fast heartbeat and poor sleep.
